metas.name: ACT Plate
metas.note: The ACT plate features equally sized blue sections on both sides with a white area in the center. This symmetry helps distinguish it from the Tasmania plate, which has more blue concentrated on the right side. For comparison, Tasmania plate on next slide.

metas.name: NSW Plate
metas.note: The easiest to recognize is the New South Wales plate, which appears purely yellow when blurred, making it easily identifiable even from a distance.

metas.name: NSW Plate – Black and White
metas.note: The New South Wales black and white plate appears slightly darker than the South Australia plate when blurred. Since both can look similar, pay attention to the surroundings—yellow plates are more common in NSW. For comparison, SA plate on next slide.

metas.name: NT Plate
metas.note: The Northern Territory plate features a bright red text on white design, similar to Queensland’s, but in a slightly lighter red. For distinction, look at the surroundings — the NT often has dry, reddish soil and sparse vegetation, giving off a distinct outback vibe compared to Queensland’s greener and more tropical feel. For comparison, Queensland plate on next slide.

metas.name: Queensland Plate
metas.note: The Queensland plate is very similar to the Northern Territory one, but uses a darker shade of red. For distinction, rely on the surrounding environment — Queensland usually feels more humid and lush, while the Northern Territory tends to look drier and more outback-like. For comparison, NT plate on next slide.

metas.name: SA Plate
metas.note: The South Australia plate is purely black and white. When blurred, it often appears black on the sides with a small white 'dot' in the center, though in certain lighting conditions it can also look entirely white. It can look like the black and white NSW plate but in a lighter white when blurred: For comparison, NSW plate on next slide.

metas.name: Tasmania Plate
metas.note: The Tasmania plate typically has more blue concentrated on the right side, while the ACT plate shows symmetrical blue sections on both sides. This subtle difference can help tell them apart when the image is blurred. For comparison, ACT plate on next slide.

metas.name: Victoria Plate
metas.note: The Victoria plate is easy to recognize thanks to its distinctive blue triangle in the center, which appears as a blue dot in the upper middle of the plate when blurred.

metas.name: WA Plate
metas.note: One of the easiest to recognize is the Western Australia plate, which features a blue horizontal bar across the top. This element remains clearly visible even when the plate is blurred.
